$comment: The validation page's list of oracle areas (item 142). Hand-written: what each area compares and which oracle it uses. Everything numeric on the page is NOT here: case counts are counted from the committed JSON named in `counts`, and a version is read from scripts/oracle/requirements.txt or from the stamp the generator wrote into the JSON. src/test/scripts/validationTools.test.ts fails when a file or test under src/test/oracle has no entry here.

areas.title: Restriction enzymes and cut sites

oracles.name: Biopython Bio.Restriction (REBASE data as Biopython ships it)

areas.compares: Where each enzyme cuts, top and bottom strand, on real plasmids, on sites straddling the origin or touching the ends of a linear molecule, and on random sequences; and that the bundled enzyme table says what REBASE says for each of its enzymes.

counts.unit: sequences cut with a panel of enzymes

areas.title: Digests, ligation and cuts at the origin

oracles.name: Biopython Bio.Restriction search(linear=False), for the cut labels at the origin

areas.compares: The top strand of every fragment and how each end looks (kind of overhang and its bases), what ligation makes of the ends (hybrid sites, blunt ends, 3' overhangs, Type IIS ends, a vector whose origin was moved), and the cut labels and fragments where a cut falls within two bases of the origin of a circle.

counts.unit: digests of random circles with a cut at the origin

areas.title: Blunted cut ends
areas.compares: A circular vector is cut, the largest fragment has its ends made blunt (T4 fill-in or mung bean trimming) and is closed on itself; the circle must equal pydna's. Sequence only: no features are carried.

areas.title: Restriction-cloning ends

oracles.name: pydna (the vector joined to the digested amplicon)

areas.compares: Where each candidate enzyme cuts the insert stretch and pUC19, and the product of cloning the insert into pUC19 with an enzyme pair, both ways round.

areas.title: PCR products

oracles.name: The textbook product (forward primer, template between, reverse complement of the reverse primer), which pydna amplify.pcr also builds

areas.compares: The product of a primer pair on linear and circular templates, across the origin, with 5' tails, inverse PCR and mismatches in the annealing part. Where pydna refuses a case (more than one binding site), only the textbook product is compared.

areas.title: Gibson, Golden Gate, overlap primers and yeast assembly
areas.compares: Each case is built backwards from a known construct and pydna must rebuild it from the same parts before it is recorded; PlasmidPop must give the same circle (up to rotation and strand). Covers Gibson, Golden Gate (BsaI, BsmBI, BbsI, SapI), In-Fusion and NEBuilder overlap primers, and yeast assembly by recombination, whose repeat warning is held to the number of circles pydna can close.

areas.title: Batch Golden Gate constructs, end to end

oracles.name: Biopython Bio.Restriction search, read for the cuts, overhangs and sites

areas.compares: The Batch page's Golden Gate rows on seeded destinations (BsaI and BsmBI, either strand, origin inside the sites), templates and regions, and on the tutorial's own rows. PlasmidPop's primers are given to pydna, which runs the tailed PCR; pydna cuts the amplicon and the destination and joins the pieces into a circle; a second circle is spliced together from Bio.Restriction's cut positions alone. PlasmidPop's construct must be that circle up to rotation and strand, with no site of the enzyme left in it or at a junction, the overhangs read off the amplicon equal to the destination's, and each primer reading padding, one site, spacer and overhang. A part that carries a site of its own, which the batch refuses to build, is confirmed when Biopython finds more than the two tail sites on its amplicon. Constructs made wrong on purpose (a base changed, deleted or added, a stretch turned round, a site planted at a junction) must be refused, and the right one turned round must be accepted.

counts.unit: controls (wrong constructs refused, right one accepted)

areas.title: Batch restriction sites, homology ends and Golden Gate extras

oracles.name: pydna amplify.pcr, Dseqrecord.cut, looped() and assembly.Assembly
Biopython Bio.Restriction search, read for the cuts, overhangs and sites

areas.compares: The Batch page's other recipes, on seeded vectors and templates and on the tutorial's own rows. Restriction sites: pydna runs the tailed PCR with PlasmidPop's primers, cuts vector and amplicon with the pair and joins the pieces; a second circle is spliced from Bio.Restriction's cut positions alone; both must be PlasmidPop's construct up to rotation and strand, the amplicon must read padding, site, extra bases, the insert, extra bases, site and padding, the construct's sites must be the vector's own plus the two the junctions rebuild, and the orientation must be the one the ligation allows (pairs in either order, a per-row enzyme pair, extra5/extra3, cloning regions across the origin, vectors read from either strand, PstI's 3-prime ends). Homology ends (In-Fusion, NEBuilder HiFi, yeast at 30, 40 and 60 bases, a kit per row): the amplicon must be the vector's end, the insert and the vector's start, and pydna Assembly on the linear vector and the amplicon must close into PlasmidPop's construct. Golden Gate: the judge of the batch-golden-gate area on rows with a second enzyme in the tube, a per-row enzyme, extra5/extra3 and left/right overhangs; a row for which the batch builds no circle is confirmed by a reason the oracle finds itself (a site of the second enzyme on the part, two cassettes both opened, overhangs that are not the destination's). Constructs made wrong on purpose must be refused and the right one turned round accepted.

counts.unit: controls (wrong constructs refused, right one accepted)

areas.title: Gateway BP and LR reactions
areas.compares: From authentic att sequences, every circle pydna makes must be one of ours (product or byproduct), up to rotation and strand, and we make no other; which of the two is the clone is checked by its bases.

areas.title: Editing, copying regions and features through a cut

oracles.name: Biopython SeqRecord slicing and reverse_complement(features=True), pydna shifted(), and a base-identity model in Python

areas.compares: One delete, insert, replace, set-origin or reverse-complement on seeded linear and circular documents with joins, both strands and features across the origin: the resulting sequence, each feature's bases and its codon_start. Also copying a region, deleting a range, and the features that survive a digest followed by a ligation.

areas.title: Genetic codes and translation

oracles.name: Biopython Bio.Data.CodonTable (the NCBI genetic codes) and Seq.translate

areas.compares: Every codon over the full IUPAC alphabet under every NCBI genetic code, start and stop codons, and whole-sequence translations.

counts.unit: genetic codes, each on every codon

areas.title: CDS translation against NCBI

oracles.name: NCBI's own /translation qualifiers on GenBank records

areas.compares: The conceptual translation of every CDS that has a protein_id in the NCBI fixtures and in ncbi-cds.gbk (small real records chosen for codon_start 2 and 3, other genetic codes, complement, join and partial ends).

areas.title: GenBank reading and location writing
areas.compares: For hand-written edge cases, records Biopython wrote, and the real NCBI fixtures: the same bases, topology and, for every feature, type, strand, qualifiers and extracted sequence; and each location written the way Biopython writes it.

areas.title: Files PlasmidPop writes, read back by other tools
areas.compares: Every GenBank and SnapGene file the writers produce for the oracle records and for randomly edited documents is read back by Biopython and compared to what was meant. Run by hand (npm run oracle:writer, oracle:snapgene-writer), because it needs Python; the result is not committed.

areas.title: FASTQ reading

oracles.name: Biopython SeqIO FASTQ parser, on Biopython's own Tests/Quality files

areas.compares: Valid files give the same record count, ids, bases and Phred qualities; truncated or ragged files are refused, as Biopython refuses them.

areas.title: AB1 chromatogram reading
areas.compares: The same base calls and qualities, and the trace channels and peaks from the tags Biopython read; a file without base calls is refused with a reason.

areas.title: SnapGene .dna reading
areas.compares: The same bases and topology, and every feature and primer at the same place on the same strand, on synthetic .dna fixtures. The sample files of a SnapGene installation can be compared locally but are not redistributed, so that run is not committed.

areas.title: Opening a region from NCBI

oracles.name: NCBI efetch, through Biopython Entrez.efetch with the same range

areas.compares: One real region (yeast HBT1 with 200 bp of flank each side, on the minus strand): the request built from esummary's placement, the same bases, and every feature's location and partial marks. The only oracle that uses the network, and only when regenerated.

areas.title: SEGUID checksums
areas.compares: SEGUID v2 (ls, cs, ld, cd) for single-stranded linear and circular sequences, double-stranded linear molecules with every mix of overhang kinds, circles on every rotation and strand, and sticky-ended fragments cut from pUC19 and pBR322.

areas.title: Melting temperature

oracles.name: primer3-py calc_tm (SantaLucia 1998, formamide and DMSO zeroed)
Biopython Tm_NN (Q5 model, Owczarzy 2004 salt correction)

areas.compares: meltingTemperature against primer3's calc_tm under five salt and primer concentrations, and q5MeltingTemperature against Biopython's Tm_NN, self-complementary primers included.

areas.title: Primer hairpins and dimers
areas.compares: The free energy of the best hairpin, self-dimer and pair dimer, and whether a primer or pair is flagged at the designer's cutoffs, against Primer3's. The gate is the share flagged the same way. The model's loop terms were fitted to data of this kind, so this set is not independent of them; item 124 reports two held-out sets as well. Also the melting temperature of each primer's best hairpin, against Primer3's, which is what Primer3 refuses a primer on.

areas.title: Primer pair selection
areas.compares: Seeded synthetic templates with a target: our designer's top five pairs for each were handed to Primer3, which says whether it would accept them and at what penalty; Primer3's own top five are recorded beside them. The gate is loose and nothing here says which of the two is right.

counts.unit: of our pairs judged by Primer3

areas.title: Pairwise alignment and read mapping
areas.compares: The optimal global and local score of seeded DNA and protein pairs and, where Biopython's best alignment is unique, the span each sequence covers; the banded path on long pairs and on pairs built to lead the band astray; read mapping across the origin of a circle against the reference written twice; and the protein effect of a variant across the origin.

counts.unit: long pairs through the banded path
reads across the origin, single and batch paths

areas.title: Multiple alignment
areas.compares: Simulated sets of related sequences (bases and proteins) along a random tree with substitutions and indels, so the true alignment is known. The share of the true alignment's residue pairs an alignment puts in one column (SP score) must reach at least 90 percent of MAFFT's mean over the sets. MAFFT is never run in the tests; the committed alignments are read.

areas.title: CRISPR guide sites

oracles.name: Biopython Bio.SeqUtils.nt_search, an independent IUPAC PAM search

areas.compares: Every guide of pUC19, pBR322, phiX174 and a linear record, and of random circles where the origin falls inside a spacer or a PAM: protospacer coordinates, the PAM, both cut boundaries, and for pUC19 off-target counts by mismatch. On-target scoring is not compared, because there is none in the app.

areas.title: Detect features
areas.compares: Real vectors from NCBI, stripped to bare sequence, annotated by pLannotate; Detect features must not fall below the recall per part class that was measured when the baseline was set, and must not name a part differently or put it on the other strand except for the listed cases. pLannotate is never run in the tests.

areas.title: Sanger read assembly

oracles.name: A known construct: reads simulated from a seeded synthetic sequence, with no external tool

areas.compares: Reads whose errors follow their own Phred qualities, over layouts with repeats and noisy ends: the contig and consensus must equal the construct, and the consensus qualities must mean what they say. Simulated reads are less realistic than real chromatograms, so a pass is a floor, not proof on real files. No data file is committed: the cases are generated inside the tests, so no case count is recorded.
